stem.en: Two genes on the same chromosome give 8 percent recombinant offspring. Two others give 40 percent. Kabir says "so the second pair of genes crosses over more easily". What does the difference mean?

text.en: The second pair of genes are further apart on the chromosome. Crossing over happens at random points; the longer the stretch between two genes, the more often a crossover lands between them. Recombinant fraction measures distance.
The second pair is on a weaker chromosome.

feedback.en: Crossing over is a normal step in every chromosome. The rate between two genes depends on their spacing.

text.en: The second pair is not really on the same chromosome.

feedback.en: Genes on different pairs give 50 percent recombinants, from independent sorting. Forty is less than fifty, so they are on the same pair, far apart.

text.en: Recombination is random and the numbers mean nothing.

feedback.en: With thousands of offspring the fractions are stable, and they add up along a chromosome like distances on a road. That is a map.

explanation.en: Crossovers land at random along the chromosome. The chance one lands between two genes grows with the distance between them. Fifty percent is the ceiling, and it equals independence.
